scenario: Space-weather monitoring stations only formally log solar-flare X-ray events exceeding 110 (in units of 10⁻⁴ W/m²), the agency alert threshold. Logged events show a mean intensity of 180 (σ=35) in those units. Solar physicists want the true mean X-ray intensity across all flare events.

data.description: Observed statistics among values exceeding the reporting threshold

values.note: Only observations above the threshold enter the record

question: (a) Assuming X-ray intensity follows a normal distribution with σ=35 10⁻⁴ W/m², solve numerically for the true population mean μ satisfying E[X | X > 110] = 180. (b) What fraction of all X-ray intensity events lie above the 110 10⁻⁴ W/m² threshold? (c) By how much (in 10⁻⁴ W/m²) does the observed truncated mean overstate the true μ? (d) Explain the inferential risk of using the observed mean directly as an estimate of μ.

ground_truth.explanation: The observed mean 180 10⁻⁴ W/m² is E[X|X>110], the expectation of a truncated-normal distribution. Solving μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=180 numerically yields μ=177.804 10⁻⁴ W/m². Only 97.4% of all events are recorded; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 2.196 10⁻⁴ W/m². Using the observed mean directly as μ would lead to systematic over-estimation of the severity/magnitude of the process.

naive_answer: The true mean X-ray intensity is 180 10⁻⁴ W/m² because that is the average of all available measurements.
naive_trap: Only events above 110 10⁻⁴ W/m² are recorded; the observed mean is a conditional expectation E[X|X>110], not the population mean. It always exceeds μ whenever the threshold is binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Define α=(t−μ)/σ where t=110, σ=35. (2) Truncated-normal expectation: E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 180 and solve for μ via brentq on [-765.0, 179.9999]. (4) Solution: μ=177.804 10⁻⁴ W/m². (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=Φ̄((110−177.804)/35)=0.97364.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 180,35,110
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-177.804)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.97364)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-2.196)<0.01
